skill.description: Search Xiaohongshu notes through SocialDataX to find examples, compare content angles, and plan topics based on a limited sample.

security_audit.summary: Most backtick hits are Markdown labels or fences, and neither the documentation URLs nor the entropy score show malicious behavior. The CLI workflow explicitly runs an unpinned npm package and gives it access to service credentials, including a persistent local key when configured. Separate concerns include unsafe keyword substitution, token-bearing links in shared outputs, and insufficient verification of billing links.

remediation.issue: Authentication and search run an unpinned npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed release, verify package integrity, and require explicit approval before downloading or running it with access to credentials.

remediation.issue: The CLI can read a persistent API key under the execution account.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer scoped credentials from a secret store. If file storage is necessary, enforce owner-only access, exclude the file from shared artifacts, and document key revocation.

remediation.issue: The shell examples do not define safe handling for user-supplied keywords.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured MCP arguments or pass the keyword as a single process argument without shell interpretation. Do not substitute it into shell source.

remediation.issue: The output rules prohibit redacting token-bearing note URLs even when sharing them.
remediation.suggestion: Use note IDs in shared outputs by default. Keep full links only when needed for authorized access, and exclude their tokens from logs and exports.

remediation.issue: The workflow can surface a billing link from an error response without a defined validation step.
remediation.suggestion: Always show the known provider billing URL and omit response-supplied links. Ask the user to verify the account and authorize any paid retry.

content.value_statement: It is hard to separate useful content patterns from noise in Xiaohongshu search results. Review a focused sample and turn visible evidence into topic ideas.
actual_capabilities: Search Xiaohongshu notes by keyword through the SocialDataX CLI or a configured MCP connection.
Filter notes by content type or publication range, and sort by recency, likes, comments, or saves.
Limit CLI results by pages or items and resume an incomplete search when a continuation cursor is available.
Report sample titles, creators, and note references when the search returns them.
Separate visible evidence from interpretations and suggest content angles and follow-up questions.
limitations: Live search requires authenticated SocialDataX access and may consume account credits.
Results reflect the returned pages, not all Xiaohongshu posts or a representative platform sample.
The CLI date filter only retains dates within the pages retrieved. It does not expand the search.
The research workflow does not publish posts, interact with notes, or modify Xiaohongshu accounts.

use_cases.title: Plan an Editorial Brief
use_cases.description: Compare recurring angles and audience questions in a small note sample before choosing topics for the next editorial cycle.

use_cases.description: Review how creators describe a product category and distinguish recurring claims from interpretations about the audience.

use_cases.title: Choose a Video Topic
use_cases.description: Review relevant video notes and use visible examples to develop an original angle for a planned post.

prompt_templates.title: Find Topic Ideas
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my configured SocialDataX MCP connection to search one page for small balcony gardens. List three relevant notes and suggest two content angles.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Recent Videos
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Add format and date filters.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my configured SocialDataX MCP connection, search for beginner meal prep videos from the past week. Sort by saves and explain what the returned examples share.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Formats
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Compare two samples using the same criteria.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my configured SocialDataX MCP connection to compare one page each of image and video notes about commuter backpacks. Use the same date range and sort order. Separate observed patterns from possible explanations.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Research Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Synthesize evidence from a bounded search.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my configured SocialDataX MCP connection to search for refillable cleaning products. Collect up to three pages using one keyword and consistent filters. Report coverage gaps, cite note IDs, and recommend three angles based on visible evidence.

output_examples.input: Review one page of recent notes about small balcony gardens.
output: Illustrative finding: Several sample titles mention rail planters and compact herb gardens.
Topic suggestion: Compare planter options for shaded rental balconies.
Coverage: The result describes one search page. It does not show how common the theme is across Xiaohongshu.

output_examples.input: Compare image and video notes about commuter backpacks.
output: Illustrative observation: Image notes show pocket layouts, while video notes demonstrate packing routines.
Interpretation: Format may influence which product details creators choose to show.
Next step: Compare similar creators and publication dates before drawing broader conclusions.

best_practices: Start with one focused keyword and one page. Expand only when the first sample cannot answer your question.
Report the filters and page limits alongside conclusions. Distinguish what the notes show from your interpretation.
Use an approved connection and confirm costs before expanding a search. Keep credentials and token-bearing links out of shared reports.
anti_patterns: Do not present one search page as evidence of a platform-wide trend.
Do not restart a partial search from the first page or change its filters while reusing a continuation cursor.
Do not paste API keys into chat or use sensitive internal terms as search keywords without approval.

faq.question: How does the skill connect to Xiaohongshu?
faq.answer: It uses the SocialDataX CLI or an authenticated SocialDataX MCP connection. It does not need a separate local CLI key when using authenticated hosted MCP.

faq.question: What details can I use to narrow my search?
faq.answer: Use a topic keyword, content type, or publication range. You can also choose a sort order such as newest or most saved.

faq.question: What can I do when the search returns no notes?
faq.answer: Broaden the keyword or remove a filter. If the search failed, check the connection or account balance before changing the query.

faq.question: Can the skill post or engage with notes?
faq.answer: No. The documented Xiaohongshu operations are for search and analysis, not posting, commenting, liking, or editing accounts.

faq.question: Does a recent search include every matching note?
faq.answer: No. A recency filter applies within the retrieved pages. Report the date window, page limit, and any partial results with your findings.

faq.question: Can I continue after a search returns partial results?
faq.answer: Keep the partial results. After resolving the error, continue only with a returned cursor, the original query settings, and the remaining page or item limit.
